question: When one issue has its body edited, its title renamed, its issue type set, changed and removed, and is closed and reopened, do the issues port's REST read of the issue and its own GraphQL query, asked back to back after each act, name one time, REST's `updated_at` GraphQL's `updatedAt`; does GitHub answer every field of the query; and does the port's `read()` read the issue whole from what they answered?
pass: Written 2026-11-20T16:25Z, before anything ran, for issue 831: pass: at each read, made after each act on one canary issue (its body edited, its title renamed, its type set, changed and removed, then closed and reopened), the port's REST read of the issue (GET /repos/{repo}/issues/{n}) and its own GraphQL query (adapters/issues.py QUERY, sent as the port sends it), asked back to back, name one time: REST's updated_at equals GraphQL's updatedAt to the second; GitHub answers the query with no errors key and every field it asks present; and the read made after the reopening, whole as adapters/issues.py read() sends it, is read by read() from the recorded exchanges with no change: its type_events the three changes, set, changed and removed, in order, each timed; content_changed_at the rename; and the Maintainer's reopening a writer's, beginning the present life. fail otherwise: if at any read the two times differ, or GitHub rejects a field of the query or leaves one out, the port's snapshot check or its query goes back to the Factory Builder before the port changes. Passed. Run on 2026-11-20 in the canary through the Maintainer's own gh login: issue 130, opened for the trial at 16:25:30Z, its body edited, its title renamed, its type set to Task, changed to Bug and removed, then closed and reopened, each by the Maintainer through REST, four or five seconds apart. After each act but the reopening the REST read and the query were asked at once, back to back; after the reopening, the read as read() sends it: the issue, its timeline, the query, the linked pull requests' query and the issue once more. At all seven reads REST's updated_at and GraphQL's updatedAt were one time to the second, and every answer to the query held every field asked and no errors key. read() reads the last read whole: three type_events, Task added, Task to Bug, Bug removed; content_changed_at the rename at 16:25:38Z, after lastEditedAt, the body's edit at 16:25:33Z; the reopening at 16:26:01Z a writer's, beginning the present life. Recorded, deciding nothing: each change of the type is timed two or three seconds after the issue's updated_at moved for it, on REST's timeline and GraphQL's alike, and a read in between gives the type already changed in REST's issue while the query lists no event for it, both naming one updatedAt: after the type was set, the issue read Task with no change of type listed; after it was changed, Bug with only the first. So the snapshot check does not catch an issue whose type and type_events disagree for those seconds. The writes (the opening, the six acts and the undo) are not recorded here, nor the permission read of the Maintainer that read() also sends. Undone after the run: issue 130 closed as not planned; nothing was minted. ran_at is the issue's opening. The issue's title and body name the trial P-71, the number it ran under; it was renumbered P-72 once another trial held P-71. Of each answer's headers only the date and the request id are kept; the redaction also removed the OAuth client id and scopes, which are no credentials.
